items.title: Kent Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I was still at that time performing with my father

ctx.x: Oh well let me mention this in the archive for you. Lu and Charlie’s was a very interesting venue. It was a club. It was owned by, oh my good friend, now Charlie Bering, who passed away maybe about six years ago. And Charlie was actually one of the producers of the Jazz and Heritage Festival but he had a club when I was in high school. And people like Alvin Batiste performed there, Ellis Marsalis performed there, all of the local New Orleans jazz giants performed there. And that was my first baptism into jazz and…

and people like James Black on drums and all these wonderful musicians. I mean I was like in heaven, I was like a child in a candy shop. You know, like studying with Ellis during the daytime and performing with people like Alvin Batiste, I was still at that time performing with my father and you know they were bringing other musicians who love New Orleans, like Cannonball Adderley —

items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: And I started that out with Kent and them. And Kent and them could hear all kinds of colors and all kinds of moving things.

ctx.x: Well I like to do more than one week so we can get them on some technical things. Go through all the scales and show them how to go from minor scales and playing diminished and half diminished chords and all of that. And to check embouchures and fingerings and all of that. That sometimes I know the teachers tell them this, but when they come from somebody else then they’ll always listen. Oh yeah he said so and so and so and so. So I’d rather do that. And have them play something by ear, a lot of stuff by ear,…

And I say all right now y’all got some harmony. And then they start switching off and doing the sections of the saxophone when we was playing. And I say, “don’t that sound good?” They say, “yeah it sounds good.” And I didn’t go through that with the trumpet section, but the saxophone section, even on “River Niger” they had their harmony going. And some other things. And I try not to do this. Just like that tune that you heard Kent spread out on [scats] “Mac the Knife.” You heard that chorale, that kind of thing?…
